title: Natural Synthetic Anomalies for Self-supervised Anomaly Detection and Localization (NSA)
mechanism: Poisson image editing blends scaled patches from other images into normal images, making natural-looking anomalies. A localiser trained on them generalises to real defects.
evidence: MVTec AD detection AUROC 97.2, best among methods without extra data. Also tested on medical images.
adaptation: Add an auxiliary head on pool cells (including the 1,152 multi half-cut cells) that predicts NSA patches made from other pool cells of the same cell type, sharing the encoder with the segmenter. The goal is a defect prior that transfers to E1. NSA patches are never labelled as background in the segmentation loss.
min_experiment: PF + NSA auxiliary head vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 crack recall@2 and relF1@2, with test crack IoU as a guard. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02.
prior_overlap: none. Anomaly-detection priors are listed as never tried. Pool MIM and DDeP were different objectives.
